title: CCI imposes penalty on Rekha Agencies and SS Marketing for indulging in anti-competitive conduct in respect of Himachal Pradesh Tender 2013 for the procurement of tyres
body_text:
The Competition Commission of India (CCI), vide an order dated 21.08.2026 issued under Section 27 of the Competition Act, 2002, (the Act) has imposed a penalty of INR 1,29,901/- on Rekha Agencies and INR 2,13,274/- on SS Marketing, for indulging in anti-competitive conduct in respect of Himachal Pradesh Tender 2013 for the procurement of tyres.
The Commission also directed Rekha Agencies and SS Marketing to cease and desist from anti-competitive conduct found to be in violation of Sections 3(3)(d) read with Section 3(1) of the Act.
Based on the contemporaneous exchange of emails containing commercially sensitive information regarding price bids before the submission of bids, the Commission found that Rekha Agencies and SS Marketing acted in a concerted manner amounting to bid rigging in Himachal Pradesh Tender 2013, thereby contravening the provisions of Section 3(3)(d) read with Section 3(1) of the Act.
The CCI also found an official of Rekha Agencies liable under Section 48 of the Act and imposed monetary penalty upon him. However, no penalty has been imposed on the official of SS Marketing as proceedings against him stood abated due to his unfortunate demise.
The order was passed in Reference Case No. 01 of 2019 and a copy of the same is available on the CCI website at www.cci.gov.in.
*****
SR/ONP

enrichment.summary: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has penalized Rekha Agencies (INR 1,29,901) and SS Marketing (INR 2,13,274) for bid rigging in a 2013 Himachal Pradesh tender for tyre procurement. The CCI found the firms exchanged commercially sensitive price-bid information before submission, violating Section 3(3)(d) read with Section 3(1) of the Competition Act, 2002. An official of Rekha Agencies was also held personally liable under Section 48, while no penalty was imposed on the SS Marketing official due to his demise.
enrichment.context: The Competition Act, 2002 prohibits anti-competitive agreements under Section 3, with Section 3(3) creating a presumption against horizontal agreements between competitors that fix prices, limit production, allocate markets, or result in bid rigging/collusive bidding (Section 3(3)(d)). Bid rigging undermines the integrity of public procurement by eliminating genuine competition, often leading to inflated costs for government contracts funded by taxpayers. Section 48 extends liability to individuals in charge of a company's affairs at the time of the contravention, ensuring that penalties are not limited to corporate entities alone. This case, though relatively small in penalty value, illustrates the CCI's continuing enforcement role against collusive practices in public tenders, a recurring issue flagged in several past CCI orders across sectors like tyres, cement, and pharmaceuticals. Such orders reinforce the importance of competitive neutrality in government procurement and serve as a deterrent against cartelization, especially given India's federal structure where state government tenders are frequent targets of bid rigging.

prelims_questions.question: Under the Competition Act, 2002, which provision deals with collusive bidding or bid rigging?
prelims_questions.explanation: Section 3(3)(d) of the Competition Act, 2002 specifically addresses agreements that result in bid rigging or collusive bidding among competitors.

prelims_questions.question: Under which section of the Competition Act, 2002 can an individual in charge of a company's affairs be held personally liable for the company's contravention?
prelims_questions.explanation: Section 48 of the Competition Act extends liability to persons responsible for the conduct of a company's business at the time of the contravention.

prelims.point: Section 3(3)(d) of the Competition Act, 2002 creates a presumption against bid rigging/collusive bidding among competitors as a form of horizontal anti-competitive agreement.
prelims.syllabus: GS Paper 2 - Statutory and Regulatory Bodies
prelims.why_important: Bid rigging under Section 3(3)(d) is a recurring CCI enforcement theme and a classic UPSC test point on distinguishing types of anti-competitive agreements.

prelims.point: Section 27 of the Competition Act empowers CCI to pass orders and impose penalties after finding a contravention of Section 3 or Section 4.
prelims.syllabus: GS Paper 2 - Statutory and Regulatory Bodies
prelims.why_important: Knowing which section grants CCI its penalty/remedial powers helps distinguish it from investigative provisions like Section 26.

prelims.point: Section 48 of the Competition Act extends liability to individuals in charge of a company's affairs at the time of contravention.
prelims.syllabus: GS Paper 2 - Statutory and Regulatory Bodies
prelims.why_important: This 'piercing the corporate veil' provision is frequently tested to check whether aspirants know liability isn't confined to the company alone.
